summary: BIOS rollback via security baseline triggers BitLocker recovery prompts on newly provisioned laptops
description:
Issue summary: After the nightly security baseline push on 2026-03-10, a subset of newly provisioned laptops entered BitLocker recovery on first user login. Impact: Affected users were blocked from completing OOBE or signing in; observed across several device SKUs and primarily in us-east. This appears correlated with an automated BIOS/firmware rollback initiated by the security baseline policy when a microcode incompatibility was detected.

Observed behavior: On reboot after config/policy apply, device shows BitLocker recovery screen requiring recovery key. Devices had been imaged via Autopilot earlier that morning and had BitLocker enabled by our provisioning script.

Expected behavior: Firmware baseline should not trigger changes to the TPM/BDE state causing BitLocker recovery; devices should remain provisionable without user intervention.
impact: ~28 devices reported so far; majority are new hires in us-east. User productivity blocked until keys retrieved. Potential for larger fleet impact if baseline continues to roll out.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Provision a device with current Autopilot image and company provisioning package.
2) Ensure BitLocker is enabled and TPM is activated during OOBE.
3) Apply security baseline containing firmware policy that includes microcode rollback rule.
4) Reboot and attempt first user sign-in.
5) Observe BitLocker recovery screen requiring recovery key.
logs: Sample BitLocker event from one device: EventID 24588 - TPM owner changed after firmware update; recovery triggered. Endpoint management audit shows baseline push at 2026-03-10T02:45:12Z. MDM job ID: MDM-20260310-8821. BiosUpdateService log: 'rollback initiated due to microcode mismatch', exit code 0x0. Attached syslog snippets saved to internal bucket (link provided in comments).
timeline:
2026-03-10 02:45 UTC - Baseline rollout started to us-east group.
2026-03-10 03:10 UTC - First BitLocker recovery reports from provisioning queue.
2026-03-10 09:00 UTC - Support ticket opened and triaged.
2026-03-11 11:30 UTC - Eng confirmed correlation with BIOS rollback action in baseline.
2026-03-12 08:20 UTC - Emergency hold placed on baseline rollout for other regions.
investigation_notes:
Hypothesis 1: Security baseline contains a firmware mitigation that attempts to rollback microcode on certain CPU SKUs which toggles TPM ownership or PCR values, causing BitLocker to enter recovery. Hypothesis 2: Our provisioning flow sets a temporary TPM owner or interacts with the TPM provisioning library; combined with rollback this changes PCRs. Verified on three devices: bios vendor logs show rollback sequence immediately before recovery prompt. No evidence of disk corruption.
Actions taken: - Paused further rollout globally. - Created reproducible test on three device SKUs in lab. - Collected MDM job details and vendor firmware logs. - Contacted BIOS vendor and Eng firmware team; vendor acknowledged rollback code path exists in their mitigation tool.
Open questions: - Why did rollback trigger on device hardware that previously passed checks? - Is there a way to apply microcode fixes without triggering TPM state changes?
workaround: For affected users: retrieve BitLocker recovery key from internal key escrow (Azure AD device object -> key escrow). IT can perform a manual BitLocker recovery with key and then re-provision TPM via our TPM provisioning runbook. For bulk recovery: a scripted recovery using Intune WinRE automation has been prepared (requires local admin and network access).
resolution_plan:
Short term: Keep baseline rollout on hold; update baseline to exclude firmware rollback rule for new-provisioning device group; run targeted canary tests on lab devices.
Medium term: Work with BIOS vendor to provide a non-TPM-impacting microcode path, or adjust our provisioning to complete TPM provisioning after firmware changes.
Post-incident: Draft runbook updates and a postmortem with action owners. Engineering will add registry/sequence checks to detect potential rollback before BitLocker enablement.
next_steps:
- Eng firmware team to deliver vendor response by 2026-03-14.
- Security baseline owner to produce emergency patch that removes rollback action for new-provisioning OU by 2026-03-12 (in progress).
- Support to run recovery/key escrow process for impacted users and track through this ticket.
- Schedule postmortem after containment complete.
